title: ENGLISH_GRADE_4___PROG_10 pronounce sounds
subject: english
text:
1 ” to allow audio playback GRADE 4 ENGLISH PROGRAMME

2 ” to allow audio playback Hello learner, welcome to a grade 4 English. Today we shall learn how to pronounce sounds and words correctly. Your radio teacher is Joyce Agik. Welcome to the program.

3 ” to allow audio playback Hello learner, welcome to grade 4 English lesson. In today’s lesson, you shall learn how to pronounce sounds and words correctly. Welcome to the lesson. Music Learner, why should we pronounce words correctly? x2 Answer when you hear the music Music Good learner. We should pronounce words correctly to communicate well. Communicating is speaking and listening to one another. Others are able to hear us clearly. Music A simile is used to compare one thing to another different thing. x2 L earner, I will read a short story. Listen carefully as I read. Identify all the similes in the story. The story is called ‘Free from Malaria’ When Jane’s mother went to the hospital, she was as afraid as a grasshopper. Her skin had become as pale as death and she had a bad cough. Her blood was as red as beetroot. The doctor took part of her blood to the laboratory. He brought the results as fast as a deer . She had malaria and was given two injections. Jane’s mother went home feeling as happy as a lark . Let me repeat the story When Jane’s mother went to the hospital, she was as afraid as a grasshopper. Her skin had become as pale as death and she had a bad cough. Her blood was as red as beetroot. The doctor took part of her blood to the laboratory. He brought the results as fast as a deer . She had malaria and was given two injections. Jane’s mother went home feelin as happy as a lark . Music Thank you learner for listening. Now I want you to identify all the similes in the story Music very good learner. The similes are: As afraid as a grasshopper. x2 As pale as death. x2 As red as beetroot x2 As fast as a deer. x2 And finally As happy as a lark. x2 learner did you hear the sound /s/ in the similes? x2 Give two more examples of similes using the sound /s/. x2 Music Thank you learner, the following are more examples. As quiet as a grave. x2 As busy as a bee. x2 Music learner, now I want you to say the words with the following sounds after me. x2 Say the words after the gong /s/- virus x2 Sfx: gong /z/-easier x2 Sfx: gong /h/-huge x2 Sfx: gong /f/-affect x2 Sfx: gong Music Thank you learner, I am going to read you a poem. Listen carefully. Write down words with the sounds /s/-/z/-/h/-/f/. -‘gh’ x2 Here I go AIDS, I have heard enough of you, You will not destroy our children, We have found a tough weapon against you, Exercise, balanced diet and medicine, You are no longer a puzzle. x2 Music Thank you learner. I hope you have written down the following sounds and words; /s/- destroy, exercise, medicine /f/- ‘gh’-enough, tough /h/-have /z/-puzzle. Music Learner, I want you to give more examples of words with the sounds /s/-/h/-/f/-/z/. x2 Music Thank you learner, I hope you gave examples as follows: /s/-sick, signs, skin x2 /f/-infect, cough, rough, x2 /h/-headache, huge, who x2 /z/-sneeze, boys, zip, x2 Music Learner, this is your homework. With the help of your parent or gurdian, try to practice pronouncing more words with the sounds we have learnt today. I hope you enjoyed the lesson. That’s the end of our lesson today. Music That was English lesson for grade four. Your radio teacher was Joyce Agik. The program was written by Joyce Agik . It was produced by Educational media directorate and recorded for the Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development. Till next time its goodbye for now.
